messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: p99 latency SLO burn in prod-eu cluster. Metric: request_p99_latency > 1200ms for 10m. Policy: SLO-Alert-Prod-EU -> page eng-oncall.

pagerduty-bot: Incident created: PD-8931. Severity: P1. Initial responders: @alex k, @sara chen. Link: https://pd.example/incidents/PD-8931

alex k: ack'd. I'm on it. Starting triage — checking region metrics and routing config.

sara chen: joining. Noticed small ramp in tokens per request earlier, but this looks like tail latency spike. Any recent deploys?

priyanka singh: no deploys in EU in last 30m from release-log. Autoscaler did a small scale-up at 12:03UTC then a few OOM logs on one node at 12:07. Could be noisy neighbor / evictions.

mike r: pulling kube events now. `kubectl -n redwood get events --field-selector type=Warning` shows repeated eviction/cgroup OOM for node eu-gpu-07.

jules: running a quick query: `sum(rate(request_duration_bucket[5m])) by (le)` shows the high tail concentrated on model-route: gpt-qlarge-v2 on eu region.

alex k: can someone check KV cache hit rates? If cache thundering occurred that could push CPU/GPU load.

priyanka singh: KV cache hitrate dropped from 92% -> 6% at spike start. Looks like cache invalidation event (redis restart?) around 12:05.

sara chen: that aligns. Autoscaler tried to spin more replicas but node evictions prevented steady capacity add -> request fanout increased latencies.

oncall-runner: Suggest immediate mitigations: 1) temporarily route EU traffic to eu-fallback-micro (lower-capacity but healthy); 2) scale up dedicated pool via manual capacity bump; 3) restart redis master only if safe. Thoughts?

alex k: I'll open a quick routing rule change to route 20% -> eu-fallback-micro as canary fallback to reduce tail. Doing it now.

alex k: (update) routing change applied: policy eu-primary -> fallback at 20%. Monitoring.

pagerduty-bot: PD-8931 update: acknowledged by alex k. Escalation policy in progress.

mike r: restarted redis replica that showed high memory churn (not master). Replica is syncing, hit rate climbing slowly. No master restart yet.

jules: after routing change p99 dropped from 1400ms -> 820ms within 2m. p95 improved too. Still some nodes showing dequeuing backlog.

priyanka singh: I'm going to cordon and drain eu-gpu-07 to avoid further evictions. Will shift loads.

sara chen: thanks. Also enabling a temporary blacklist for large-batch requests on gpt-qlarge-v2 in EU to prevent heavy tails. Patch applied.

alex k: PD notes: customer-impact: some interactive endpoints may have experienced suboptimal latency for ~12:02-12:10UTC. No data loss.

oncall-runner: handing off to next on-call in 30m. If things look stable, we'll un-wind routing after 1 hour and keep an eye.

priyanka singh: eu-gpu-07 drained successfully, pods rescheduled on eu-gpu-09 and eu-gpu-10. Redis replica fully synced. KV hit rate back to ~88%.

jules: p99 now at 330ms. I'll keep a watch dash for 30m before closing PD.

alex k: closing notes for the thread: root cause: simultaneous KV cache disruption (redis replica restart) + node-level evictions causing autoscaler instability -> temporary capacity gap and request fanout -> p99 spike. Mitigations: routing fallback, replica restart, node drain. Follow-ups: add autoscaler backoff/coordination with cache resync, add alert for KV hitrate drop to avoid noisy pages.

pagerduty-bot: PD-8931 status updated to resolved (post-mortem pending).

sara chen: creating postmortem ticket: PM-482 on our tracker. cc @product-sre @infra.

alex k: thumbs up. Good triage everyone. :thumbsup:
